name: Tridens

project_scope.note: Only three Tridens species are manifest-backed; historical source-pool names may map to Tridentopsis. All three retain provisional range labels.

look_here_first: TRIDENS: start with a multi-flowered spikelet in a terminal panicle. At a glance WHITE TRIDENS (T. albescens) is narrow, dense and upright; PURPLETOP (T. flavus) is generally large and openly branched, often drooping; TEXAS TRIDENS (T. texanus) has slender flexuous branches with hanging groups of spikelets—NOT a tight spike. Next dissect a mature SPIKELET: paired GLUMES, 3-NERVED LEMMAS and exact NERVE HAIR distribution settle overlaps. Purple color and bare branch bases are not species-level tests.
shared_traits: Perennial grasses with panicles of multi-flowered spikelets
Glumes and three-nerved lemmas useful for confirmation

comparison_matrix.albescens: Dense, narrow and mostly upright, appressed branches
comparison_matrix.flavus: Wide, long and open, usually spreading or drooping
comparison_matrix.texanus: Flexuous open to moderately open, shorter and drooping; not a true compact spike

comparison_matrix.flavus: Frequently red-purple fresh, turning pale/tan at maturity
comparison_matrix.texanus: Frequently rose-purple, becomes straw colored; not decisive

comparison_matrix.character: Bare proximal sections of lateral branches
comparison_matrix.texanus: Often conspicuous; same basic character occurs in purpletop

comparison_matrix.albescens: About 4–10 (Kew), larger counts in other descriptions
Nearly equal glumes ~4 mm; maturity/scale needed
comparison_matrix.flavus: Glumes shorter than whole multi-flowered spikelet; count intact parts
comparison_matrix.texanus: Glumes often about half as long as individual lemmas

comparison_matrix.albescens: Glabrous or basal hairs only (review mature lemma)
comparison_matrix.flavus: Nerve hairs extend over lower part; requires true macro
comparison_matrix.texanus: Usually hairy along three nerves below middle; requires true macro

comparison_matrix.albescens: Green and straw mature appressed narrow heads
comparison_matrix.flavus: Open purple head and open dry tan panicles, shared empty branch bases
comparison_matrix.texanus: Arching flexuous axis, bare branch sections, rose-marked overlapping spikelets

overlap_cautions: The provisional T. texanus species record says narrow panicle; regional flora describes flexuous branches bare basally. Needs targeted review.
Panicle length and plant height overlap; confirm glume and lemma anatomy.
Historical Tridens buckleyanus, eragrostoides and muticus source-pool names require accepted-concept mapping; do not add duplicate species cards.

Bare proximal panicle-branch segments occur in both T. flavus and T. texanus; do not use their presence as a standalone couplet. Pair complete panicle architecture with dissected glume:lemma proportions and lemma-nerve pubescence.
diagnostic_photo_checklist: One whole rooted panicle for each species at same scale, with fresh and dry state documented
Whole panicle side views of both T. flavus and T. texanus showing proximal branch gaps
Each species mature unbroken 4–13 mm spikelet with 1-mm ruler and 4–12+ florets counted
Detach each species paired glumes versus one intact fertile lemma and record relative lengths
Detached dorsal lemma under 10–20×: count THREE nerves and exact distribution of hairs
True leaf collar ligule and basal sheath of same voucher, avoiding unverified images

0.question: Resolve panicle-architecture conflict in T. texanus species record and confirm current Tridens/Tridentopsis accepted concepts; bare branch bases are shared with T. flavus, not a unique key character. Do not change range in this genus lane.

1.question: No action until existing source-pool historical names are taxonomically mapped; do not install duplicate Tridens/Tridentopsis concepts.

2.question: Prioritize exact-species macro photographs of glume:lemma proportions, lemma hairs, and panicle-branch bases; retain provenance.

handoffs.manual_tridens_followup: Acquire individually licensed/source-determined diagnostic macro evidence for lemma nerves/glumes/collar. No reason to repeat canonical admission or native range. Keep any county status unchanged.

species_differences.first_check: Dense, lance-shaped narrow panicle with branches tightly appressed to axis; head varies green, white and purple.
species_differences.confirm: Paired glumes nearly equal (~4 mm), fertile lemmas almost glabrous or hairy only at base. Examine on measured mature material.
species_differences.caution: Panicle color is unreliable; the two real photos show green and pale ripe forms.

species_differences.first_check: Broadly open arching or drooping panicle, often comparatively tall; flowering spikelets can be red, late heads tan.
species_differences.confirm: Short hairy ligule, flattened basal sheaths and hairy lemma nerve lines are supporting anatomy; glumes need careful comparison to Texas tridens.
species_differences.caution: Bare lower sections of flowering branches ALSO occur in T. texanus; the new late dry image documents color loss.

species_differences.first_check: Flexuous, OPEN to moderately open, often shorter panicle with bare proximal stretches on lateral branches and terminal grouped spikelets.
species_differences.confirm: Glumes roughly half as long as lemmas; lemma three nerves pubescent below middle. Often 6–12 florets.
species_differences.caution: Do not say 'compact narrow spike'; existing photographs show arching exposed branches and T. flavus shares the empty branch bases.

visual_lesson.title: Tridens — 3 photographed grasses, then separate their reproductive parts
visual_lesson.status: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS: true head morphology arrowed in six real photos; mature lemma macro remains missing
visual_lesson.look_here_first: TRIDENS: start with a multi-flowered spikelet in a terminal panicle. At a glance WHITE TRIDENS (T. albescens) is narrow, dense and upright; PURPLETOP (T. flavus) is generally large and openly branched, often drooping; TEXAS TRIDENS (T. texanus) has slender flexuous branches with hanging groups of spikelets—NOT a tight spike. Next dissect a mature SPIKELET: paired GLUMES, 3-NERVED LEMMAS and exact NERVE HAIR distribution settle overlaps. Purple color and bare branch bases are not species-level tests.

steps.title: 1 · Look at the whole panicle
steps.plain: Dense and narrow albescens, broadly open flavus, or flexuous often shorter texanus?
steps.where: Entire flowering stalk / head, not a trimmed branch
steps.why: Good first clue across 6 verified visible photos; juvenile or late-season heads may differ

steps.title: 2 · Compare basal sections of the panicle branches
steps.plain: Look for a bare stem segment before the first seed units.
steps.where: Base of the lateral branches in flavus and texanus
steps.why: BOTH species may have it; annotating it helps teach a common false-positive
steps.photo_role: Dry T. flavus and full mature T. texanus panels

steps.title: 3 · Separate an actual mature spikelet
steps.plain: Find the two outer glumes, then compare lemma size and count the fertile florets.
steps.where: Unbroken ripe spikelet beside millimeter ruler
steps.why: Glumes nearly equal in albescens; about half lemma in texanus; check whole spikelet/lemma ratios with an actual specimen
steps.photo_role: All three mature detached spikelet macros needed

steps.title: 4 · Follow the three lemma nerves
steps.plain: Check where fine hairs run along the three raised lines on the lemma back.
steps.where: Detached mature dorsal lemma at 10–20× (use more magnification if necessary)
steps.why: Almost bald albescens versus hairier flavus and lower-nerve-hairy texanus
steps.photo_role: All three species matched lemma hair closeups

steps.title: 5 · Confirm collar and sheath
steps.plain: Lift blade at its stem junction and look for a very short hairy ligule; document sheaths at base.
steps.where: Leaf collar and rooted tuft of same specimen
steps.why: Supports Tridens versus visually similar grasses and flowering-stage comparisons
steps.photo_role: All three collar macro views needed

comparison_cards.title: White tridens versus purpletop
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Dense, narrow versus broad open panicle; confirm by basal sheath and lemma hair patterns.
comparison_cards.caution: Panicle color is variable; photograph whole stalk and dissected lemma.

comparison_cards.title: Texas tridens versus purpletop
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Compare complete panicle architecture at the same scale, then dissect mature spikelets to check glume:lemma proportions and hair placement on lemma nerves.
comparison_cards.caution: Both may show spikelet-free proximal panicle branches. Do not use bare branch sections as an exclusive distinction; panicle lengths overlap.

comparison_cards.title: Texas tridens versus lovegrasses
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Dissect spikelet for Tridens lemma nerve architecture rather than relying on pinkish seedhead color.
comparison_cards.caution: Eragrostis secundiflora can resemble T. texanus in the field.

visual_comparison.title: TRIDENS — white tridens, purpletop and Texas tridens in six real photos
visual_comparison.subtitle: Two existing locally archived rights-tagged original photographs per species, annotated only where gross structures really show. Photos are references rather than independently verified vouchers.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: WHITE = narrow packed; PURPLETOP = open broad; TEXAS = flexuous separated. Always confirm glume/3-nerve lemma; bare branch bases overlap.
